text: Six months since Antonio died. The house still smells like his pipe tobacco in the study. I sat in his chair for an hour.
Signed up for the Thursday watercolour class at the library. The teacher, Bernard, is very patient. My first painting looked like a puddle.
The knee is worse. Stairs are an ordeal. Dr. Moreau wants an X-ray.
Mateo and Sofia stayed the weekend. We made empanadas and Sofia ate the filling straight from the bowl. Mateo is quiet these days, nearly a teenager.
X-ray results: arthritis, and the joint is badly worn. Dr. Moreau mentioned a knee replacement. I said I'd think about it. I'm terrified.
Watercolour class. Painted the harbour. Bernard said my sky had 'feeling'. I think he says that to everyone but I took it anyway.
Mrs. Hale from next door brought round a casserole and stayed two hours. She lost her husband too, years ago. We talked about the first year.
Carmen called. She thinks I should sell the house and move nearer to her and the children. I hung up a bit sharply. I'm not ready.
Bad day. Found Antonio's reading glasses in the coat pocket. Couldn't stop crying. Didn't go to class.
Said yes to the knee operation. The waiting list is about three months. Dr. Moreau says the pain should be much better after.
Apologised to Carmen for being sharp. She cried too. She worries. We agreed to talk about the house again in the summer, not now.
Painted Antonio's old fishing boat from a photograph. Bernard didn't say anything, just put his hand on my shoulder.
Mateo phoned me himself, no prompting from Carmen, to ask how to make my lentil soup. I nearly dropped the phone.
The knee kept me awake most of the night. Took the stronger painkillers. Hate how foggy they make me.
Mrs. Hale and I have started walking to the market together on Saturdays. Slowly, with my stick. She talks, I listen, it suits us both.
The library is putting on an exhibition of the class's work. Bernard chose my harbour painting. I've told everyone, including the postman.
Lonely evening. The television was talking and nobody was listening. Thought about calling Carmen and didn't.
Exhibition opening. Carmen brought the children. Sofia told strangers 'my abuela painted that'. Best day in a long time.
Pre-op assessment at the hospital. Blood tests, a lot of forms, a nurse called Precious who made me laugh about my veins.
Sorted through Antonio's clothes finally. Kept the green jumper. Gave the rest to the church sale. Mrs. Hale helped me fold.
Operation day. Last thing I remember is the anaesthetist asking about my grandchildren.
Woke up with a new knee and a lot of pain. The physio had me standing on day one. Brutal woman. Kind eyes.
Home from hospital. Carmen is staying for a week. She's rearranged my kitchen and I'm too sore to object.
Physio exercises three times a day. They hurt. I do them anyway, mostly. Mrs. Hale comes round to count for me like a sergeant major.
Walked to the end of the garden without the frame. Small thing. Sat on the bench and grinned at the roses.
Carmen raised the house again, gently. A bungalow near her, no stairs. With the new knee the stairs are less of a reason, but she's right that I'm alone a lot.
Back at watercolour class for the first time since the operation. Bernard had kept my place by the window. Painted badly and happily.
Mateo came on his own on the bus to visit. Thirteen now. We made the lentil soup together and he told me about a girl in his class.
Physio signed me off. Six weeks ahead of schedule, she said. I walked to the market and back with Mrs. Hale and only stopped once.
Antonio's birthday. Took flowers to the cemetery and told him about the knee, the painting, the boy. Sad but peaceful.
Went to see a bungalow near Carmen. Light, small, a garden for roses. I didn't hate it. That surprised me.
Couldn't sleep thinking about the move. This house is forty years of us. The bungalow is a future. Both are true.
Told Mrs. Hale I might move. She went quiet and then said she'd visit by bus every week. I believe her.
Made the offer on the bungalow. Carmen cried on the phone. So did I. Then I painted for three hours.
Sofia drew a picture of 'Abuela's new house' with a rainbow and a cat I don't have. Pinned it on the fridge.
Offer accepted. Started sorting the attic. Found our wedding album. Sat on the attic floor and laughed at Antonio's moustache.
